skill.name: backend-hang-debug
skill.description: Diagnose FastAPI backend hangs caused by blocking ThreadPoolExecutor shutdown in SSE news streams.
skill.summary: Debug FastAPI event-loop hangs with py-spy triage and a non-blocking executor shutdown pattern.
skill.author: BenderFendor

security_audit.summary: The skill is procedural FastAPI debugging guidance, and many Markdown backtick detections are false positives for code identifiers or localhost checks. Confirmed risks remain for /proc inspection, socket enumeration, py-spy stack dumps, and sudo process attachment. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Privileged py-spy process dumps are recommended in the debugging flow.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before any py-spy or sudo command, and explain that stack dumps can expose sensitive runtime data.

remediation.issue: py-spy is installed without a pinned version before privileged use.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a trusted py-spy version or ask users to install it through their normal approved dependency process before debugging.

remediation.issue: The triage commands enumerate listening sockets and inspect /proc for a running process.
remediation.suggestion: Scope these checks to the target development environment, avoid automatic execution, and avoid copying process metadata into shared logs.

content.value_statement: FastAPI streams can hang when executor shutdown blocks the event loop. This skill gives a triage and fix path using py-spy, curl checks, and a non-blocking shutdown pattern.
actual_capabilities: Diagnoses FastAPI event-loop hangs linked to blocking ThreadPoolExecutor shutdown.
Guides localhost health checks for root and health endpoints.
Uses py-spy stack capture to identify blocked main-thread frames.
Describes a non-blocking executor shutdown pattern for SSE stream handlers.
Provides retest checks for client aborts and backend responsiveness.
limitations: Focused on FastAPI, uvicorn, SSE streams, and RSS worker behavior.
Requires access to the backend process and local development environment.
Some diagnostic steps may need elevated permissions and explicit approval.
Does not replace full production observability or incident response procedures.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a stalled FastAPI service
use_cases.description: Find whether an SSE route is blocking the event loop after a client disconnects.

use_cases.title: Validate service recovery after stream aborts
use_cases.description: Run bounded health checks and confirm the backend stays responsive during stream failures.

use_cases.title: Document a safe executor pattern
use_cases.description: Capture a repeatable fix for avoiding blocking shutdown in async stream handlers.

prompt_templates.title: Check a basic hang
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a local backend that stops responding.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use backend-hang-debug to triage a local FastAPI app that times out on root and health checks. Explain each check before suggesting any command.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect stream disconnect behavior
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate debugging for an SSE route after client aborts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my FastAPI SSE stream handler for blocking executor shutdown after a client disconnect. Recommend the smallest code change and retest steps.

prompt_templates.title: Compare stack evidence to source code
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced diagnosis using process stack evidence.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have py-spy stack output showing ThreadPoolExecutor shutdown on the main thread. Map the evidence to the likely source code path and propose a fix.

prompt_templates.title: Create a guarded remediation plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a remediation plan for a FastAPI news stream hang. Include approval gates for privileged diagnostics, code changes, rollout checks, and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: A FastAPI service times out after an SSE news stream is opened and aborted.
output_examples.output: The likely cause is blocking executor shutdown in the stream generator. The next step is to confirm responsiveness with local health checks, then inspect stack evidence only with approval.

output_examples.input: Stack evidence shows the main thread waiting inside ThreadPoolExecutor shutdown.
output_examples.output: Replace the short-lived executor context manager with a long-lived executor and non-blocking shutdown. Retest by aborting the stream and checking that health endpoints still respond.

output_examples.input: A team needs a release checklist for the backend hang fix.
output_examples.output: The checklist should include before-and-after health checks, client abort testing, stack verification, RSS timeout review, and a rollback step for the stream route change.

best_practices: Ask for approval before running py-spy, sudo, or process inspection commands.
Record before-and-after health check results for each debugging session.
Keep RSS network timeouts bounded so worker threads cannot block indefinitely.
anti_patterns: Running privileged debugger commands automatically from a marketplace skill.
Changing executor logic without reproducing the hang and retesting client abort behavior.
Treating localhost health checks as proof that all stream concurrency issues are fixed.

faq.question: What problem does this skill address?
faq.answer: It helps diagnose FastAPI hangs caused by blocking executor shutdown in an SSE news stream route.

faq.question: Does it run py-spy automatically?
faq.answer: No. py-spy use should be reviewed and approved because it can inspect live process state.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it target?
faq.answer: It targets FastAPI with uvicorn, ThreadPoolExecutor usage, SSE streams, and RSS ingestion workers.

faq.question: Can it debug production incidents?
faq.answer: It can guide investigation, but production use needs normal approval, access control, and incident procedures.

faq.question: What is the main code pattern it recommends?
faq.answer: It recommends non-blocking executor shutdown so stalled worker threads do not freeze the event loop.

faq.question: Why are localhost curl checks included?
faq.answer: They provide quick evidence that the root and health endpoints remain responsive after stream activity.
